newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Russia negative on West's bid for trade freeze.
newsitem.headline: Russia negative on West's bid for trade freeze.

text.p: A senior Russian official said on Wednesday it would be difficult to implement a freeze sought by the West on tougher trade measures while Moscow is negotiating entry to the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

The official, deputy foreign trade minister Georgy Gabuniya, was quoted by trade sources as making his remarks at a meeting of the WTO working party discussing Russia's four-year-old bid to join the 130-member body.

The four top trading powers -- the United States, the European Union, Japan and Canada -- called on Moscow for a "standstill" in introducing any new trade restrictive measures when the working party opened its two-day session on Tuesday.

The sources said Gabuniya argued that given his country's "deep-going economic reform" it would be impractical to implement a standstill -- which would also bar measures that would give it extra leverage in the entry discussions.

Many WTO members are concerned at what they see as a lack of coordination between Moscow ministries and official bodies like the customs which they say often take decisions making access to the Russian market more difficult for foreign goods.
U.S. Assistant Trade Representative Dorothy Dwoskin told the working party on Tuesday that Russia "should move towards consistency with the (WTO) rules...."

The sources said Gabuniya, whose ministry had a new chief chief appointed on Wednesday by President Boris Yeltsin to replace the returning minister Oleg Davydov, argued the key issue was that Russia was committed to market reform.
Any changes in its trade policy, he added, would be taken "with the logic of the market in mind."
A standstill -- which has been pledged by China in its own decade-long negotiations to join the WTO -- would only be possible if there were a static trading situation in the country.
